short_description.id: Naga Chuvash atau Verechelen adalah ular api dalam legenda orang Chuvash yang dapat terbang, menyemburkan api, dan menjelma manusia.
short_description.en: The Chuvash dragon, or Verechelen, is a fire serpent of Chuvash legend that can fly, breathe fire and take human form.

long_description.id: Verechelen atau naga Chuvash adalah naga dalam legenda orang Chuvash yang dapat terbang, menyemburkan api, dan berubah wujud; dalam legenda ia tokoh jahat yang sering menjelma suami atau istri yang telah meninggal. Satu jenisnya, Věri Şělen, berkepala banyak dan meninggalkan jejak api saat terbang, seperti Gorynych dari Rusia.
long_description.en: Verechelen, the Chuvash dragon, is a dragon of Chuvash legend that can fly, breathe fire and change shape; in legends it is a negative figure that often takes the form of a dead spouse. One kind, Věri Şělen, has many heads and leaves a fiery trail in flight, like the Russian Gorynych.

long_description.en: One source glosses its name "invisible snake" and says it reflects the mythology of Volga Bulgaria, unlike the Zilant. Religious scholar A. K. Salmin rejects the explanation that the name means "fire snake". In the founding legend of Bilär, a great snake there asked Allah for wings and flew away.

short_description.id: Cikavac adalah makhluk mitos dalam mitologi Serbia, dibayangkan sebagai burung berparuh panjang dengan kantong seperti pelikan, yang mencuri madu dan susu untuk pemiliknya.
short_description.en: The cikavac is a mythical creature of Serbian mythology, imagined as a long-beaked bird with a pelican-like pouch that steals honey and milk for its owner.

long_description.id: Cikavac adalah makhluk mitos dalam mitologi Serbia, dibayangkan sebagai hewan bersayap (burung) dengan paruh panjang dan kantong seperti pelikan. Seekor cikavac dapat diperoleh dengan mengambil telur ayam betina hitam, yang lalu dibawa seorang perempuan di bawah ketiaknya selama 40 hari; selama itu ia tidak boleh mengaku dosa, memotong kuku, membasuh muka, atau berdoa.
long_description.en: The cikavac is a mythical creature of Serbian mythology, imagined as a winged animal (a bird) with a long beak and a pelican-like pouch. A cikavac could be had by taking an egg from a black hen, which a woman then carried under her armpit for 40 days, during which she must not confess, cut her nails, wash her face or pray.

long_description.id: Setelah menetas, cikavac mengisap madu dari sarang lebah orang lain dan susu dari ternak orang lain, lalu membawanya kepada pemiliknya. Ia memenuhi setiap keinginan pemiliknya dan membuat pemiliknya mengerti bahasa hewan. Di Republik Ceko, plivník adalah makhluk kecil yang memainkan peran serupa.
long_description.en: Once hatched, the cikavac sucked honey from other people's beehives and milk from other people's cattle and brought it to its owner. It fulfilled the owner's every wish and let the owner understand the language of animals. In the Czech Republic the plivník is a sprite that plays the same role.

short_description.id: Iblis Boruta adalah tokoh iblis dalam mitologi, cerita rakyat, dan sastra Polandia yang dikaitkan dengan kota Łęczyca, perubahan wujud leshy pagan Slavia setelah Kristenisasi.
short_description.en: Devil Boruta is a devil figure of Polish mythology, folklore and literature associated with the town of Łęczyca, a post-Christian transformation of the pagan Slavic leshy.

long_description.id: Iblis Boruta adalah tokoh dari mitologi, cerita rakyat, dan sastra Polandia yang dikaitkan dengan kota Łęczyca; ia dikatakan tinggal di ruang bawah tanah kastel Łęczyca. Tokoh ini merupakan perubahan wujud leshy pagan Slavia pada masa setelah Kristenisasi, dan juga disebut błotnik, roh rawa. Linde mendefinisikannya sebagai roh jahat yang menurut dongeng petani tinggal di rawa dan tempat berlumpur.
long_description.en: Devil Boruta is a figure of Polish mythology, folklore and literature tied to the town of Łęczyca; he is said to live in the vaults beneath Łęczyca castle. The figure is a post-Christianisation transformation of the pagan Slavic leshy, and is also called błotnik, a swamp spirit. Linde defined him as an evil spirit that, by peasant tales, lives in swamps and muddy places.

long_description.id: Ia biasanya dianggap bangsawan yang sibuk merusak para bangsawan, digambarkan sebagai szlachcic tinggi berkumis hitam panjang dengan kontusz yang menutupi ekornya dan topi yang menutupi tanduknya. Namun ia juga muncul sebagai burung bersayap besar, ikan bertanduk, kuda hitam, burung hantu, serigala, dan penggiling. Dalam semua legenda ia sangat licik dan bertenaga melebihi manusia, tetapi dalam banyak legenda ia juga dermawan yang membagikan tepung kepada orang miskin. Zygmunt Gloger dan sejumlah etnolog menganggap Boruta berpakaian bangsawan sebagai folklor palsu abad ke-19.
long_description.en: He was usually thought of as a nobleman busy corrupting nobles, shown as a tall szlachcic with long black moustaches, a kontusz hiding his tail and a cap hiding his horns. Yet he also appeared as a great-winged bird, a horned fish, a black horse, an owl, a wolf and a miller. In all legends he is very cunning and superhumanly strong, but in many he is also a benefactor who gives flour to the poor. Zygmunt Gloger and some ethnologists held the noble-dressed Boruta to be 19th-century fakelore.

short_description.id: Lou Drapé adalah kuda hantu dari Aigues-Mortes, Prancis selatan, yang pada malam hari mengumpulkan anak-anak tersesat di punggungnya yang terus memanjang lalu membawa mereka pergi selamanya.
short_description.en: Lou Drapé is a ghostly horse of Aigues-Mortes in southern France that gathers lost children at night on its ever-lengthening back and carries them off for good.

long_description.id: Lou Drapé adalah kuda legendaris Aigues-Mortes di rawa Petite Camargue. Pada malam hari ia berkeliaran di sekitar tembok kota dan mengumpulkan anak-anak tersesat di punggungnya, yang memanjang hingga muat lima puluh sampai seratus anak; anak-anak itu tidak pernah kembali. Kuda pucat ini lambang kematian dan dipakai untuk menakuti anak, mungkin versi drac Occitania yang dapat berwujud kuda.
long_description.en: Lou Drapé is a legendary horse of Aigues-Mortes in the Petite Camargue marshes. At night it roams the town walls and gathers lost children on its back, which stretches to hold fifty or a hundred; the children never return. This pale horse is a symbol of death used to frighten children, perhaps a version of the Occitan drac that can take horse form.

long_description.id: Collin de Plancy mencatatnya pada 1818, dan pada 1965 anak-anak masih ditakut-takuti dengannya. Menurut Frédéric Mistral drapet berarti drac kecil, tetapi asal nama Lou Drapé tidak diketahui pasti. Konon anak terakhir yang menungganginya membebaskan semua anak dengan menyerukan Yesus, Maria, dan Santo Yosef. Ia termasuk kelompok kuda penculik yang terkait air, seperti drac Pyrenees.
long_description.en: Collin de Plancy recorded it in 1818, and in 1965 children were still threatened with it. Frédéric Mistral says drapet means a small drac, but the name's origin is uncertain. The last child to ride it is said to have freed them all by calling on Jesus, Mary and Saint Joseph. It belongs to a family of water-linked kidnapping horses, like the Pyrenean drac.

short_description.id: Drekavac, "si penjerit", adalah makhluk mitos Slavia Selatan, sering dianggap arwah anak yang mati sebelum dibaptis, yang keluar dari kubur pada malam hari.
short_description.en: The drekavac, "the screamer", is a South Slavic mythical creature, often held to be the soul of a child who died unbaptised, rising from the grave at night.

long_description.id: Drekavac, yang namanya berarti "si penjerit" dan diturunkan dari kata kerja drečati, adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Slavia Selatan dengan nama lain seperti drekalo, krekavac, zdrekavac, dan zrikavac. Legendanya terutama dikenal di Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kroasia, dan Montenegro. Menurut anggapan yang tersebar luas, ia adalah arwah bayi yang mati tanpa dibaptis.
long_description.en: The drekavac, whose name means "the screamer" and comes from the verb drečati, is a creature of South Slavic mythology also called drekalo, krekavac, zdrekavac and zrikavac. Its legend is found mainly in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Montenegro. In the common view it is the soul of an infant who died unbaptised.

long_description.id: Wujudnya digambarkan sangat beragam. Dalam sebagian cerita ia lelaki mayat hidup yang keluar dari kubur pada malam hari untuk menghantui orang hidup; dalam cerita lain ia anak yang belum dibaptis yang menghantui orang tuanya dan memohon kepada orang yang lewat di dekat kuburan agar membaptisnya. Di Serbia timur ia berupa makhluk anjing mirip manusia yang berjalan dengan kaki belakang, di sekitar Arilje makhluk berleher dan berkaki panjang dengan kepala seperti kucing, dan di sekitar Gruža makhluk bertubuh belang, panjang, dan kurus dengan kepala terlalu besar yang tidak bisa terbang.
long_description.en: Its form is described in many ways. In some tales it is an undead man who leaves his grave at night to haunt the living; in others it is an unbaptised child that haunts its parents and begs passers-by near cemeteries to baptise it. In eastern Serbia it is a humanlike canine walking on its hind legs, around Arilje a long-necked, long-legged creature with a cat-like head, and around Gruža a dappled, long, spindly creature with an oversized head that cannot fly.

long_description.id: Pada mulanya drekavac dipercaya berasal dari jiwa orang berdosa atau anak yang mati tanpa dibaptis. Ia diyakini hanya tampak pada malam hari, terutama pada dua belas hari Natal dan awal musim semi, ketika setan dan makhluk mitos lain dianggap lebih aktif. Dalam rupa anak ia meramalkan kematian seseorang, dalam rupa hewan ia meramalkan penyakit ternak; ia menghindari anjing dan cahaya terang, dan siapa pun yang terkena bayangannya akan sakit lalu meninggal.
long_description.en: The drekavac was first thought to come from the souls of sinful men or of children who died unbaptised. It was believed to be visible only at night, above all during the twelve days of Christmas and in early spring, when demons and other mythical beings were held to be more active. In the shape of a child it foretells a death, in animal shape a cattle disease; it shuns dogs and bright light, and anyone its shadow falls on will sicken and die.

long_description.id: Kini drekavac terutama dipakai dalam cerita peringatan untuk anak-anak, walau ada orang dewasa yang masih memercayainya. Pada 1992 penduduk Krvavica menemukan sisa bangkai hewan yang tidak dikenal dan menyebutnya drekavac, tetapi kemudian ternyata itu hanya bangkai rubah yang membusuk.
long_description.en: Today the drekavac is mostly used in cautionary tales for children, though some adults still believe in it. In 1992 villagers in Krvavica found the remains of an unfamiliar animal and called it a drekavac, but it later proved to be only a rotting fox carcass.

short_description.id: Fenodyree adalah makhluk gaib berbulu dalam folklor Pulau Man, sejenis peri yang membantu pekerjaan manusia seperti brownie.
short_description.en: The fenodyree is a hairy supernatural being of Isle of Man folklore, a fairy that helps people with their chores, much like a brownie.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Pulau Man (Isle of Man), fenodyree adalah makhluk gaib berbulu, sejenis peri (Manx: ferrishyn), yang kerap mengerjakan pekerjaan berat untuk manusia, mirip brownie di Skotlandia dan Inggris. Ia mengangkut balok batu besar dan memotong rumput padang dengan kecepatan luar biasa, sehingga dijuluki yn foldyr gastey, "si pemotong rumput yang gesit". Hadiah pakaian justru membuatnya pergi.
long_description.en: In the folklore of the Isle of Man the fenodyree is a hairy supernatural being, a kind of fairy (Manx ferrishyn), that often does heavy work for people, comparable to the brownies of Scotland and England. It hauls huge blocks of stone and cuts meadow grass astonishingly fast, earning the name yn foldyr gastey, 'the nimble mower'. A present of clothes, however, makes it leave.

long_description.id: Joseph Train dan J. F. Campbell mengartikan namanya "yang berbulu". Ada penulis yang menyebutnya raksasa yang lebih kuat dari manusia, tetapi I. H. Leney menyebut tingginya dua kaki. Dalam satu kisah ia dulunya ksatria Istana Peri yang diubah menjadi berwujud mirip satir sebagai hukuman karena jatuh cinta pada gadis manusia dari Glen Aldyn dan melewatkan pesta panen. Kisah terkenalnya, "The Fynoderee of Gordon", diterbitkan Sophia Morrison pada 1911. Artikel de mencatat cerita bahwa ia pernah mencoba mengangkut air dengan saringan.
long_description.en: Joseph Train and later J. F. Campbell glossed the name as 'the hairy one'. Some authors call it a giant stronger than any man, while I. H. Leney gives its height as two feet. One tale makes it a former knight of the Fairy Court, changed into a satyr-like shape as a penalty for courting a mortal girl of Glen Aldyn and missing the harvest festivities. Its best-known story, 'The Fynoderee of Gordon', was printed by Sophia Morrison in 1911. The de article adds a tale of it trying to carry water in a sieve.

long_description.id: Ular api, dalam bahasa Rusia ognennyi zmei dan Ukraina vohnyanyy zmiy, adalah makhluk jahat dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, sering iblis atau roh yang berubah wujud. Dalam tradisi Slavia Timur ia umumnya tampak seperti pikulan menyala, sapu yang terbakar, atau bola api biru yang memercikkan bunga api saat terbang; gambaran ini dikaitkan dengan bola api meteor, bintang jatuh, atau meteorit. Di Rusia ia juga disebut zmey lyubak, nalotnik ("penyerbu"), dan letun ("penerbang").
long_description.en: The fiery serpent, Russian ognennyi zmei and Ukrainian vohnyanyy zmiy, is a wicked being of Russian folk belief, often a demon or spirit in changed form. In East Slavic tradition it usually looks like a blazing carrying-pole, a burning broom or a glowing ball of blue fire throwing off sparks as it flies; this image has been tied to bolides, shooting stars and meteorites. In Russia it also goes by names such as zmey lyubak, nalotnik ("raider") and letun ("flyer").

long_description.id: Ia menjalin hubungan seksual dengan perempuan, yang berakibat sakit dan kematian sang perempuan, dan berwujud ganda: di udara sebagai ular api bersayap, di bumi sebagai manusia. Ular api sering merupakan perwujudan mayat yang datang kepada istri atau perempuan yang dicintainya. Di Ukraina, perelesnyk adalah iblis berwujud ular api (meteor) yang terbang menuju perempuan.
long_description.en: It has sexual relations with women, leading to their illness and death, and has a double form: a fiery winged serpent in the air and a man on the ground. The fiery serpent is often the guise of a walking dead man who comes back to his wife or beloved. In Ukraine the perelesnyk is a demon in the form of a fiery snake (a meteor) that flies to women.

short_description.id: Guivre atau vouivre adalah naga berwujud ular bernapas racun dari legenda Prancis abad pertengahan, agresif tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang.
short_description.en: The guivre or vouivre is a serpentine, venom-breathing dragon of medieval French legend, aggressive yet afraid of naked humans.

long_description.id: Guivre, givre, atau vouivre adalah nama Prancis untuk makhluk mitis berwujud ular yang setara dengan lindworm atau wyvern; namanya berasal dari kata Latin vipera, dan kata Inggris wyvern berasal darinya. Ia bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kadang bertanduk, bernapas racun, dan tinggal di kolam, danau, hutan, dan tempat lembap. Ia sangat agresif tetapi tersipu dan memalingkan muka bila melihat manusia telanjang.
long_description.en: Guivre, givre or vouivre is the French name for a serpentine mythical creature equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern; the name comes from Latin vipera, and English wyvern comes from it. It has a long serpentine body and dragon's head, sometimes horns, venomous breath, and lives in pools, lakes, forests and damp places. It is highly aggressive yet blushes and looks away on seeing a naked human.

long_description.id: Dalam heraldik vouivre disebut guivre, dan di Lorraine, Bourgogne, Franche-Comté, Jura, serta Swiss ia naga berkaki dua atau ular bersayap yang membawa batu merah delima di dahinya. Dalam kisah Santo Samson dari Dol, Santo Suliao mengeluarkan seekor guivre kecil dari jubah imam yang tamak, lalu mengusirnya.
long_description.en: In heraldry the vouivre is called guivre, and in Lorraine, Burgundy, Franche-Comté, the Jura and Switzerland it is a two-legged dragon or winged serpent bearing a carbuncle on its brow. In the tale of Samson of Dol, Saint Suliao pulls a small guivre from a greedy priest's robe and exorcises it.

short_description.id: Hircocervus atau tragelaphos adalah makhluk khayalan setengah kambing setengah rusa yang dipakai Platon dan Aristoteles sebagai contoh sesuatu yang dapat dibayangkan tetapi tidak ada.
short_description.en: The hircocervus or tragelaph is an imaginary half-goat, half-stag that Plato and Aristotle used as an example of something imaginable but non-existent.

long_description.id: Hircocervus, dari bahasa Latin hircus "kambing jantan" dan cervus "rusa jantan", atau tragelaphos dalam bahasa Yunani, adalah makhluk khayalan setengah kambing setengah rusa. Dalam Republik, Sokrates menyamakan pemikirannya dengan pelukis kambing-rusa, dan Aristoteles memakainya sebagai contoh hal yang dapat dijelaskan tetapi tidak ada; Boethius menerjemahkannya menjadi hircocervus. Diodorus Siculus justru menganggapnya hewan nyata.
long_description.en: The hircocervus, from Latin hircus 'billy goat' and cervus 'stag', or tragelaphos in Greek, is an imaginary half-goat, half-stag. In the Republic Socrates compares his thinking to painters of goat-stags, and Aristotle used it as an example of something describable yet non-existent; Boethius translated it as hircocervus. Diodorus Siculus, though, treated it as a real animal.

long_description.id: Kata ini masuk bahasa Inggris pada 1398, dipakai Martin Luther pada 1540 untuk hukum yang tidak menghukum, dan kemudian menjadi kiasan untuk hal yang mustahil. Buffon mengenali tragelaphos Plinius sebagai rusa tua bersurai panjang.
long_description.en: The word entered English in 1398, was used by Martin Luther in 1540 for a law that does not condemn, and later became a figure for anything absurd. Buffon identified Pliny's tragelaph as an old long-maned stag.

statement.en: The hircocervus (Latin hircus, 'billy goat' + cervus, 'stag') or tragelaph (Greek), also called goat-stag, was a legendary creature imagined as half goat, half stag.

statement.en: In Plato's Republic, Socrates likens his image-making to painters who paint goat-stags by combining features of different things (488a).

claims.quote: In his work De Interpretatione, Aristotle utilized the idea of a fabulous goat-stag to express the philosophical concept of something that is describable even though it does not really exist. His Greek "τραγέλαφος" was rendered into Latin "hircocervus" by Boethius.

statement.id: Dalam De Interpretatione, Aristoteles memakai kambing-rusa dongeng untuk menjelaskan konsep sesuatu yang dapat dijelaskan walau tidak benar-benar ada; Boethius menerjemahkan kata Yunaninya menjadi hircocervus.
statement.en: In De Interpretatione Aristotle used the fabulous goat-stag to express something describable though non-existent; Boethius rendered his Greek word into Latin as hircocervus.

claims.quote: On the other hand, Diodorus Siculus treats the tragelaphos as an existing animal, and there are references in Greek literature to other hybrid creatures such as the hippelaphos (horse-stag).

statement.id: Sebaliknya, Diodorus Siculus memperlakukan tragelaphos sebagai hewan yang benar-benar ada, dan sastra Yunani juga menyebut hibrida lain seperti hippelaphos (kuda-rusa).
statement.en: Diodorus Siculus, by contrast, treats the tragelaphos as a real animal, and Greek literature mentions other hybrids such as the hippelaphos (horse-stag).

claims.quote: The word hircocervus first appears in the English language in a medieval manuscript dating from 1398 (now at the Bodleian Library).

statement.id: Kata hircocervus pertama muncul dalam bahasa Inggris pada naskah abad pertengahan tahun 1398 yang kini di Bodleian Library.
statement.en: The word hircocervus first appears in English in a medieval manuscript of 1398, now in the Bodleian Library.

claims.quote: Martin Luther uses the term "tragelaphus" in his Theses Against the Antinomians (1540, Sixth Set) to describe "a law that does not condemn".

statement.id: Martin Luther memakai istilah tragelaphus dalam Tesis Melawan Kaum Antinomian (1540) untuk menggambarkan "hukum yang tidak menghukum".
statement.en: Martin Luther used 'tragelaphus' in his Theses Against the Antinomians (1540) for 'a law that does not condemn'.

statement.en: According to the French article, Pliny's tragelaph is probably the same as Aristotle's hippelaphos, and Buffon identified both as an old stag whose neck grows long hair so that from afar it looks like a horse.

short_description.id: Hydrus adalah ular air dari bestiari abad pertengahan yang menyusup ke mulut buaya yang tidur lalu merobek perutnya dari dalam, lambang Kristus yang keluar dari neraka.
short_description.en: The hydrus is a water snake of medieval bestiaries that slips into a sleeping crocodile's mouth and tears its belly from inside, an emblem of Christ breaking out of Hell.

long_description.id: Hydrus, juga disebut Enhydros atau Ydrus, adalah makhluk bestiari Abad Pertengahan yang biasanya dianggap ular air, tetapi juga digambarkan sebagai burung, naga, atau luwak. Menurut Aberdeen Bestiary namanya berasal dari kata Yunani untuk air karena ia hidup di Sungai Nil. Plinius Tua menyebut bisanya paling kuat di antara ular, dengan hati sebagai penawarnya, dan Thomas dari Cantimpré menyebut gigitannya menimbulkan "penyakit boa".
long_description.en: The hydrus, also called Enhydros or Ydrus, is a creature of Medieval bestiaries usually taken as a water snake but also shown as a bird, dragon or mongoose. The Aberdeen Bestiary derives its name from the Greek for water because it lives in the Nile. Pliny the Elder called its venom the strongest of any snake, its liver the cure, and Thomas of Cantimpré said its bite causes the 'boa sickness'.

long_description.id: Hydrus membenci buaya: ia berlumur lumpur, menyelinap ke mulut buaya yang tidur, lalu merobek perutnya dari dalam. Tradisi Kristen menjadikannya lambang Kristus yang turun ke dunia orang mati dan bangkit, seperti dalam Bestiaire de Gervaise. Ia kadang dicampuradukkan dengan Hydra dari mitos Yunani.
long_description.en: The hydrus hates crocodiles: it coats itself in mud, slips into a sleeping crocodile's mouth and rips open its belly from inside. Christian tradition made it a symbol of Christ descending to the dead and rising, as in the Bestiaire de Gervaise. It is sometimes confused with the Hydra of Greek myth.

role.en: Kills crocodiles from inside.

description.id: Bisanya lebih kuat dari ular mana pun; hatinya menjadi penawar.
description.en: Its venom is stronger than any snake's; its liver is the antidote.

note.en: Sometimes confused with it.

claims.quote: The Hydrus (also known as Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris, and Ydrus) is a creature from Medieval bestiaries.

statement.id: Hydrus (juga Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris, dan Ydrus) adalah makhluk dari bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: The Hydrus (also Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris and Ydrus) is a creature of Medieval bestiaries.

claims.quote: A hydrus has no set appearance. Normally it is considered to be a water snake. Other animals the hydrus has been thought of as include a bird, a dragon, and a mongoose.

statement.id: Wujud hydrus tidak tetap; biasanya ia dianggap ular air, tetapi juga digambarkan sebagai burung, naga, atau luwak.
statement.en: The hydrus has no fixed look; it is usually taken to be a water snake, but also shown as a bird, a dragon or a mongoose.

claims.quote: Pliny the Elder described the hydrus as a amphibious serpent with stronger venom than any other snake. He also says that the hydrus' liver can be used as an antidote to its bite.

statement.id: Plinius Tua menggambarkan hydrus sebagai ular amfibi dengan bisa lebih kuat dari ular mana pun, dan hatinya dapat dipakai sebagai penawar gigitannya.
statement.en: Pliny the Elder described the hydrus as an amphibious serpent with venom stronger than any other snake's, whose liver can serve as an antidote to its bite.

claims.quote: They were said to be found in the Nile River. It is said that the hydrus hated crocodiles, and would intentionally roll in the mud and seek out a crocodile while it slept with its mouth open.

statement.id: Hydrus konon hidup di Sungai Nil dan membenci buaya; ia sengaja berguling di lumpur lalu mencari buaya yang tidur dengan mulut terbuka.
statement.en: They were said to live in the Nile and to hate crocodiles; the hydrus would roll in mud on purpose and seek out a crocodile sleeping with its mouth open.

claims.quote: Once inside the crocodile's stomach, the hydrus would burst free from the stomach lining, ripping out the crocodile's entrails and leaving it to die. In medieval Christian tradition, this bursting free from the crocodile became an emblem of the resurrection of Christ bursting free from Hell.

statement.id: Di dalam perut buaya, hydrus merobek dinding perut dan isi perut buaya itu hingga mati; dalam tradisi Kristen abad pertengahan, hal ini menjadi lambang kebangkitan Kristus yang keluar dari neraka.
statement.en: Inside the crocodile's stomach the hydrus tears free through the lining and entrails, leaving it to die; in medieval Christian tradition this became an emblem of Christ's resurrection breaking out of Hell.

short_description.id: Iku-Turso adalah makhluk mitologi Finlandia yang merujuk pada satu atau beberapa raksasa; dalam Kalevala ia monster laut yang jahat.
short_description.en: Iku-Turso refers to one or more giants of Finnish mythology; in the Kalevala it is a malevolent sea monster.

long_description.id: Iku-Turso, juga dikenal sebagai Iku-Tursas, Meritursas, Tursas, atau Turisas, merujuk pada satu atau beberapa raksasa dalam mitologi Finlandia, dan dalam Kalevala ia tampil sebagai monster laut yang jahat. Nama Turisas kemungkinan kata pinjaman awal dari bahasa Proto-Jermanik yang berarti "raksasa". Para ahli belum sepakat apakah berbagai penyebutan Tursas dalam lagu-lagu runik merujuk pada satu makhluk atau beberapa.
long_description.en: Iku-Turso, also called Iku-Tursas, Meritursas, Tursas or Turisas, refers to one or several giants of Finnish mythology, and in the Kalevala appears as a malevolent sea monster. The name Turisas is probably an early loan from Proto-Germanic meaning "giant". Scholars do not agree whether the various mentions of Tursas in runic songs mean one being or several.

long_description.id: Wujudnya tidak pasti, tetapi ia dikaitkan dengan sejumlah julukan: partalainen ("yang tinggal di tepi" atau "yang berjanggut"), Tuonen härkä ("lembu Tuoni"), tuhatpää ("berkepala seribu"), dan tuhatsarvi ("bertanduk seribu"). Satu lagu menyebut Meri-Tursas ("Tursas Laut") menghamili Loviatar, Gadis dari Utara, melalui ombak ketika ia mencari kelegaan di air, sehingga Loviatar melahirkan penyakit-penyakit dunia.
long_description.en: Its looks are uncertain, but epithets attached to it include partalainen (a dweller on the brink, or else a bearded one), Tuonen härkä (Tuoni's ox), tuhatpää (having a thousand heads) and tuhatsarvi (having a thousand horns). One song tells how Meri-Tursas, "Sea Tursas", impregnated Loviatar, the Maiden of North, through the waves as she sought relief in the water, so that she gave birth to the diseases of the world.

long_description.id: Dalam daftar dewa Tavastia yang disusun Mikael Agricola pada 1551, Turisas disebut dewa perang yang memberi kemenangan. Ada usulan bahwa dewa itu sama dengan Tyr, dewa perang Skandinavia, tetapi teori ini kini tidak banyak didukung. Menurut Anna-Leena Siikala, Turisas dan Tursas mungkin semula dua makhluk berbeda yang kemudian tercampur dalam lagu-lagu runik.
long_description.en: In the list of Tavastian gods compiled by Mikael Agricola in 1551, Turisas is named as the god of war who brought victory. It has been suggested that this god is the same as the Scandinavian war god Tyr, but the theory is not widely supported today. According to Anna-Leena Siikala, Turisas and Tursas were probably originally two different beings who became mixed in runic songs.

short_description.id: Konrul adalah burung raksasa berumur panjang dalam mitologi Turkik yang lahir kembali seperti phoenix dan menolong pahlawan dengan bulunya.
short_description.en: Konrul is a giant, long-lived bird of Turkic mythology that is reborn like the phoenix and helps heroes with its feathers.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Turkik, Konrul adalah burung berumur panjang yang terus-menerus lahir kembali, seperti phoenix. Ia digambarkan cukup besar untuk membawa gajah, berwujud merak berkepala anjing dan bercakar singa, kadang berwajah manusia. Ia bermusuhan dengan ular, hidup di tempat yang banyak air, dan memiliki kembaran bernama Toghrul.
long_description.en: In Turkic mythology Konrul is a long-lived bird that is reborn again and again, like the phoenix. It is pictured as big enough to carry off an elephant, a peacock with a dog's head and lion's claws, sometimes with a human face. It is hostile to snakes, lives where water is plentiful and has a twin named Toghrul.

long_description.id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang pahlawan membunuh ular yang hendak memangsa anak-anak Konrul. Sebagai hadiah ia menerima tiga bulu untuk dibakar bila butuh pertolongan, dan Konrul kemudian membawanya ke negeri jauh. Dalam kisah lain Konrul membawa pahlawan keluar dari dunia bawah.
long_description.en: In one tale a hero kills a serpent about to eat Konrul's young. As a reward he receives three feathers to burn when he needs help, and Konrul later carries him to a distant land. In another tale Konrul carries the hero out of the underworld.

short_description.id: Lí Ban adalah perempuan yang menjadi putri duyung dalam legenda terbentuknya Lough Neagh, Irlandia, kemudian dibaptis sebagai Santo Muirgen.
short_description.en: Lí Ban is a woman turned mermaid in the legend of the forming of Lough Neagh, Ireland, later baptised as Saint Muirgen.

long_description.id: Lí Ban atau Liban (dari bahasa Irlandia Kuno lí "kecantikan" dan ban "perempuan", berarti "teladan para perempuan") adalah perempuan yang menjadi putri duyung dalam legenda terbentuknya Lough Neagh. Keluarganya tenggelam saat danau besar itu menyembur, tetapi ia selamat setahun dalam ruang di bawah air, lalu berubah menjadi setengah manusia setengah salem. Menurut kisah Aided Echach maic Maireda dalam Lebor na hUidre abad ke-12, danau itu dinamai menurut ayahnya, Eochaid mac Mairidh.
long_description.en: Lí Ban or Liban (Old Irish lí, 'beauty', and ban, 'of women', so 'paragon of women') is a woman turned mermaid in the legend of how Lough Neagh came to be. Her family drowned when the great lake burst up, but she lived a year in an underwater chamber and then became half woman, half salmon. In the tale Aided Echach maic Maireda in the 12th-century Lebor na hUidre, the lake takes its name from her father Eochaid mac Mairidh.

long_description.id: Dalam wujud putri duyung ia terlihat oleh kapal yang membawa utusan St. Comgall ke Roma, berjanji bertemu di Inbhear nOllarbha (Larne Lough) setahun kemudian, dan tertangkap jaring. Ia dibaptis Comgall dengan nama Muirgein ("lahir dari laut") atau Muirgeilt, dan tercatat sebagai Santo Muirgen dengan hari raya 27 Januari. Annals of the Four Masters mencatat penangkapannya pada 558 M. Artikel fi menyebutnya memilih langsung ke surga setelah dibaptis.
long_description.en: In mermaid form she was seen from the ship carrying St. Comgall's messenger to Rome, promised to meet at Inbhear nOllarbha (Larne Lough) a year later, and was caught in a fishnet. Comgall baptised her Muirgein ('sea-born') or Muirgeilt, and she is listed as Saint Muirgen with a feast on 27 January. The Annals of the Four Masters date her capture to 558 AD. The fi article says that after baptism she chose to go straight to heaven.

role.en: Became a saint.

short_description.id: Lubber fiend atau Lob adalah makhluk legenda folklor Inggris yang mirip brownie, roh rumah yang mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah tangga.
short_description.en: The lubber fiend, or Lob, is a creature of English folklore resembling the brownie, a household spirit that does chores.

long_description.id: Lubber fiend, juga Lob, lubberkin, lurdane atau Lob Lie-By-The-Fire, adalah makhluk legenda folklor Inggris yang mirip brownie (atau Urisk) Skotlandia, hob Inggris utara, domovoi Slavia dan tomte Skandinavia; ia juga dikaitkan dengan Robin Goodfellow. Ia terkenal karena disebut John Milton dalam puisi pastoral "L'Allegro". Biasanya ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki besar berbulu dan berekor yang mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah dengan imbalan semangkuk susu dan tempat di depan perapian.
long_description.en: The lubber fiend, also Lob, lubberkin, lurdane or Lob Lie-By-The-Fire, is a being of English folklore akin to the brownie (or Urisk) of Scotland, the hob of northern England, the Slavic domovoi and the Scandinavian tomte, and has been linked with Robin Goodfellow. John Milton's mention of it in the pastoral 'L'Allegro' is its best-known appearance. It is usually a big hairy man with a tail who does the housework in return for a saucer of milk and a spot by the fire.

long_description.id: Satu kisah menyebutnya putra raksasa seorang penyihir dan Iblis. Abbey lubber adalah setan kecil yang menghantui gudang anggur dan dapur biara, menggoda para biarawan untuk mabuk, rakus dan bernafsu; kisahnya yang paling terkenal adalah Friar Rush. Lob juga muncul dalam karya Edward Thomas, Juliana H. Ewing dan J. M. Barrie, serta dalam The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt sebagai roh pelindung rumah.
long_description.en: One story makes it the giant offspring of a witch and the Devil. The abbey lubber is a lesser demon that infests abbey wine cellars and kitchens, luring monks into drinking, gluttony and lust; Friar Rush is the best-known abbey lubber tale. short_description.id: Manipogo adalah monster danau dalam cerita rakyat Kanada yang konon hidup di Danau Manitoba, digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular dengan punuk.
short_description.en: Manipogo is a lake monster of Canadian folklore said to live in Lake Manitoba, described as a serpent-like creature with a hump.

long_description.id: Manipogo adalah monster danau yang konon hidup di Danau Manitoba, Kanada. Namanya meniru Ogopogo dari British Columbia. Ia digambarkan bertubuh cokelat kehitaman dengan sedikitnya satu punuk di atas air; kepalanya disamakan dengan kepala kuda, unta, atau domba, atau disebut pipih berbentuk belah ketupat. Saat muncul ke permukaan, ia konon menjerit.
long_description.en: Manipogo is a lake monster said to live in Lake Manitoba, Canada. Its name echoes British Columbia's Ogopogo. It is described as brownish-black with at least one hump above the water; its head is likened to a horse's, camel's or sheep's, or said to be flat and diamond-shaped. It reportedly shrieks as it surfaces.

long_description.id: Penduduk First Nations setempat sudah lama punya legenda tentang makhluk mirip ular di danau itu. Penampakan pertama yang terdokumentasi oleh pemukim kulit putih dilaporkan pedagang bulu Valentine McKay pada September 1909. Pada 1936 nelayan Oscar Fredrickson konon menjaring sebuah tengkorak hewan, tetapi tengkorak itu hilang ketika rumahnya terbakar.
long_description.en: Local First Nations people have long told of serpent-like creatures in the lake. The first documented sighting by a white settler was reported by fur trader Valentine McKay in September 1909. In 1936 fisherman Oscar Fredrickson reportedly netted an animal skull, but it was lost when his house burned down.

long_description.id: Sebagian skeptis menduga yang terlihat sebenarnya rusa moose yang berenang. Makhluk ini memberi nama Taman Provinsi Manipogo, dan komunitas St. Laurent mengadakan Festival Manipogo setiap minggu pertama Maret.
long_description.en: Some sceptics think witnesses saw a swimming moose. The creature gives its name to Manipogo Provincial Park, and the community of St. Laurent holds a Manipogo Festival every first week of March.

role.en: A creature reported in sightings since 1909.

short_description.id: Michigan Dogman adalah makhluk mirip anjing berkaki dua dalam legenda modern Michigan, yang menurut catatan berawal dari lagu lelucon April Mop Steve Cook tahun 1987.
short_description.en: The Michigan Dogman is a two-legged dog-like creature of modern Michigan legend which, by the record, began with Steve Cook's 1987 April Fool's song.

long_description.id: Michigan Dogman digambarkan sebagai anjing berkaki dua setinggi 2,1 m bertubuh manusia dengan lolongan seperti jeritan manusia, yang konon pertama terlihat pada 1887 di Wexford County dan muncul setiap tahun berakhiran tujuh. Namun catatan yang terdokumentasi berawal pada 1987, ketika Steve Cook memutar lagu The Legend sebagai lelucon April Mop; Cook mengaku mengarangnya sendiri, dan klaim legenda Odawa tidak pernah punya sumber autentik.
long_description.en: The Michigan Dogman is described as a 2.1 m two-legged canine with a man's torso and a scream-like howl, said to have been first seen in 1887 in Wexford County and to return in years ending in seven. But the documented record begins in 1987, when Steve Cook played his song The Legend as an April Fool's joke; Cook said he invented it, and the claimed Odawa legend has no authentic source.

long_description.id: Setelah lagu itu, banyak pendengar mengaku bertemu makhluk serupa. Kriptozoologi menggolongkannya makhluk mirip anjing yang berjalan tegak, sedangkan folkloris menganggapnya legenda regional modern.
long_description.en: After the song, many listeners claimed to have met such a creature. Cryptozoology classes it as an upright canid, while folklorists treat it as a modern regional legend.

who.en: A two-legged canine with a man's torso.

claims.quote: In folklore, the Michigan Dogman is an alleged creature first witnessed in 1887 in Wexford County, Michigan, United States. It was described as a seven-foot-tall (2.1 m), blue- or amber-eyed bipedal canid possessing the torso of a man with a fearsome howl resembling a human scream.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, Michigan Dogman adalah makhluk yang konon pertama terlihat pada 1887 di Wexford County, Michigan, Amerika Serikat, digambarkan sebagai anjing berkaki dua setinggi tujuh kaki (2,1 m) bermata biru atau kuning, bertubuh manusia, dengan lolongan seperti jeritan manusia.
statement.en: In folklore the Michigan Dogman is an alleged creature first seen in 1887 in Wexford County, Michigan, United States, described as a seven-foot (2.1 m), blue- or amber-eyed two-legged canine with a man's torso and a howl like a human scream.

claims.quote: Folklore claims that the creature reemerges on a recurring ten-year pattern linked to years ending in the number seven.

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat, makhluk ini muncul kembali setiap sepuluh tahun pada tahun yang berakhiran angka tujuh.
statement.en: Folklore says the creature reappears every ten years, in years ending in seven.

claims.quote: In 1987, disc jockey Steve Cook at WTCM-FM in Traverse City, Michigan, recorded a song titled "The Legend", which he initially played as an April Fool's Day joke.

statement.id: Pada 1987 penyiar radio Steve Cook di WTCM-FM, Traverse City, merekam lagu The Legend yang mula-mula diputar sebagai lelucon April Mop.
statement.en: In 1987 disc jockey Steve Cook of WTCM-FM in Traverse City recorded a song, The Legend, first played as an April Fool's joke.

claims.quote: I made it up completely from my own imagination as an April Fools' prank for the radio and stumbled my way to a legend that goes back all the way to Native American times.

statement.id: Cook mengaku mengarang lagu itu sepenuhnya dari imajinasinya sebagai lelucon April Mop untuk radio.
statement.en: Cook said he made it up entirely from his own imagination as an April Fools' prank for the radio.

claims.quote: After he played the song, Cook received calls from listeners who said that they had encountered a similar creature.

short_description.id: Muladona adalah bagal betina berkepala perempuan dari mitologi Katalan, gadis terkutuk yang menyusup ke rombongan bagal pada malam hari dan membuat mereka berlari ke jurang.
short_description.en: The Muladona is a woman-headed female mule of Catalan mythology, a cursed girl who slips into mule trains at night and drives them over ravines.

long_description.id: Muladona atau Donamula, "bagal-perempuan", adalah gadis yang dikutuk warga desanya menjadi bagal karena tidak hormat dan tidak beragama. Ia tampak seperti bagal tetapi bersurai seperti rambut perempuan, berwajah manusia, dan berpayudara. Pada malam hari ia bergabung dengan rombongan bagal di pegunungan sehingga bagal-bagal ketakutan dan jatuh ke jurang.
long_description.en: The Muladona or Donamula, 'mule-woman', is a girl her townsfolk cursed into a mule for being irreverent and irreligious. She looks like a mule but has a woman's hair for a mane, a human face and breasts. At night she joins mule trains in the mountains, so the mules panic and fall into ravines.

long_description.id: Kusir bagal memberi hewannya roti berbentuk Muladona agar tidak takut, dan terus menghitung bagal mereka agar ia tidak menyusup tanpa ketahuan.
long_description.en: Muleteers fed their animals Muladona-shaped bread so they would not take fright, and kept counting their mules so she could not slip in unseen.

role.en: Frightens mule trains.

description.id: Bagal yang makan roti ini tidak takut kepadanya.
description.en: Mules fed this bread are not frightened of her.

claims.quote: In Catalan mythology, a Muladona or Donamula (mule-woman or woman-mule in Catalan) is a female mule with a human woman's head. Legend has it that a young woman was cursed by the townspeople for being irreverent and irreligious, and the curse turned her into a mule.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, Muladona atau Donamula ("bagal-perempuan") adalah bagal betina berkepala perempuan; menurut legenda, seorang gadis yang tidak hormat dan tidak beragama dikutuk warga desanya menjadi bagal.
statement.en: In Catalan mythology the Muladona or Donamula ('mule-woman') is a female mule with a woman's head; by legend a young woman cursed by her townsfolk for being irreverent and irreligious was turned into a mule.

claims.quote: According to legend, she wandered mountains, especially at night, joining mule trains. It was claimed that mules were frightened by her presence enough to stampede into ravines and die.

statement.id: Ia berkeliaran di pegunungan, terutama malam hari, dan bergabung dengan rombongan bagal, yang ketakutan hingga berlari ke jurang dan mati.
statement.en: She roamed the mountains, especially at night, joining mule trains, whose mules were so frightened they stampeded into ravines and died.

claims.quote: The Muladona looks like a mule, but it is a mixture of human and animal, its mane is like a woman's hair and its face, while still appearing to be like that of an animal, is obviously human.

statement.id: Muladona tampak seperti bagal tetapi campuran manusia dan hewan: surainya seperti rambut perempuan dan wajahnya, walau seperti hewan, jelas manusia.
statement.en: The Muladona looks like a mule but is a mix of human and animal: her mane is like a woman's hair, and her face, though animal-like, is clearly human.

claims.quote: It is always represented with the four legs of a mule, but sometimes the front two legs join a thorax, located where a mule would have its neck. In addition, the animal is always represented with breasts to underline that it is female.

statement.id: Ia selalu digambarkan berkaki empat bagal, kadang dengan kaki depan menyatu pada dada manusia di tempat leher bagal, dan selalu berpayudara untuk menegaskan bahwa ia perempuan.
statement.en: She is always shown with a mule's four legs, sometimes with the front legs joined to a chest where a mule's neck would be, and always with breasts to stress she is female.

claims.quote: The muleteers used to give their mules small Muladona-shaped pieces of bread to eat, in the belief that this would stop the animals being frightened and allow them to ignore her if she appeared.

statement.id: Para kusir bagal memberi bagal mereka roti kecil berbentuk Muladona agar hewan itu tidak takut dan mengabaikannya bila ia muncul.
statement.en: Muleteers fed their mules little Muladona-shaped breads so the animals would not take fright and would ignore her if she appeared.

claims.quote: Así y todo, durante la marcha contaban las cabezas que llevaban para evitar que la muladona se hubiese mezclado con sus animales sin que ellos se diesen cuenta y acabasen pagándolo caro.

statement.en: According to the Spanish article, during the journey they kept counting their animals so the Muladona would not slip in among them unnoticed.

short_description.id: Nekomata adalah yōkai kucing dalam cerita rakyat Jepang yang biasanya digambarkan memiliki ekor bercabang dua.
short_description.en: Nekomata is a cat yōkai in Japanese folklore usually depicted with a tail split in two.

long_description.id: Nekomata adalah yōkai yang dikisahkan berasal dari kucing tua atau besar. Ciri yang sering disebut ialah ekor bercabang dua. Dalam sebagian kisah ia berjalan dengan dua kaki, berbicara seperti manusia, dan mengganggu orang. Ada pula tradisi yang menempatkannya sebagai makhluk pegunungan berbahaya. Gambaran ini menunjukkan bahwa kisah nekomata tidak hanya tentang kucing peliharaan di rumah.
long_description.en: Nekomata are yōkai said to arise from old or large cats. A familiar sign is a tail divided in two. Some accounts have them walk on two legs, speak human language, and cause mischief. Other traditions place them among dangerous mountain creatures. The stories therefore extend beyond household cats.

long_description.id: Dalam seni Jepang, nekomata tampil sebagai kucing berekor bercabang yang menari pada dua kaki, termasuk dalam gambar Toriyama Sekien. Sebuah kajian koleksi seni mengingatkan bahwa batas antara nekomata dan bakeneko sering kabur. Satu kisah daerah Nakanomata di Niigata menuturkan seorang penduduk mengalahkan nekomata, sedangkan legenda Gunung Nekomata di Toyama mengisahkan makhluk yang menyerang manusia. Beragam contoh ini menunjukkan perkembangan penggambarannya dalam seni dan cerita setempat.
long_description.en: In Japanese art, nekomata appear as fork-tailed cats dancing on two legs, including in images by Toriyama Sekien. A study of an art collection notes that the boundary between nekomata and bakeneko is often unclear. A Niigata story tells of a villager defeating a nekomata, while a Toyama mountain legend tells of a creature that attacked people. These examples show their varied roles in art and local stories.

short_description.id: Oilliphéist adalah ular laut atau monster mirip naga dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Irlandia, yang konon mengukir alur Sungai Shannon.
short_description.en: The Oilliphéist is a sea serpent or dragon-like monster of Irish myth and folklore said to have carved the course of the River Shannon.

long_description.id: Oilliphéist (dari oll "besar" dan péist "cacing, binatang ajaib, monster, reptil") adalah ular laut atau monster mirip naga dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Irlandia (Irish). Monster-monster ini diyakini menghuni banyak danau dan sungai di Irlandia (Ireland), dan ada banyak legenda tentang orang suci dan pahlawan yang melawan mereka. Dalam satu kisah, Sionnan, cucu Manannán mac Lir, membuat marah Salmon of Knowledge dengan melemparinya batu, dan ikan itu memanggil seekor Oilliphéist yang akhirnya membunuhnya.
long_description.en: Its name joining oll, 'great', to péist, a word for worm, beast or monster, the Oilliphéist is a dragon-like sea serpent of Irish legend. Such monsters were believed to live in many Irish lakes and rivers, and many legends tell of saints and heroes fighting them. One tale tells how Sionnan, a granddaughter of Manannán mac Lir, pelted the Salmon of Knowledge with stones; in revenge the fish summoned an Oilliphéist, which killed her.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah lain, seekor Oilliphéist mengukir alur Sungai Shannon dan danau-danau di dekatnya ketika mendengar bahwa Santo Patrick datang untuk mengusirnya: ia berangkat dari Shannon Pot, membentuk Lough Allen, dan melahap domba serta sapi penduduk. Penduduk dekat Athleague melawannya dipimpin peniup pipa mabuk bernama O'Rourke, yang ditelan monster itu tetapi terus bermain pipa di dalam perutnya selama berhari-hari hingga dimuntahkan. Menurut artikel pt, Ollphéist adalah sekelompok monster laut yang kadang digambarkan bercirikan naga, ular, atau serangga, di selatan disebut Ollpiasta, dan kadang dapat terbang atau berbicara.
long_description.en: In another tale an Oilliphéist carves the course of the Shannon and nearby lakes on hearing that Saint Patrick has come to drive it out: setting off from Shannon Pot, it forms Lough Allen and devours the locals' sheep and cattle. People near Athleague stand against it led by a drunken piper named O'Rourke, whom it swallows; he keeps piping in its stomach for days until it coughs him up. According to the pt article Ollphéist names a group of sea monsters sometimes given dragon, snake or even insect traits, called Ollpiasta in the south, and at times able to fly or speak.

role.en: Driven out by Saint Patrick.

short_description.id: Ördög adalah makhluk iblis pengubah wujud dalam mitologi dan paganisme awal Hungaria yang menguasai kekuatan gelap dan jahat di dunia.
short_description.en: Ördög is a shape-shifting demonic being of Hungarian mythology and early paganism who controls the dark and evil forces of the world.

long_description.id: Ördög, dalam bahasa Hungaria Kuno Ürdüng, adalah makhluk iblis pengubah wujud dari mitologi dan paganisme awal Hungaria yang menguasai kekuatan gelap dan jahat di dunia. Setelah Kristenisasi ia disamakan dengan Iblis. Dalam mitologi Hungaria, Isten (Tuhan) dibantu Ördög saat menciptakan dunia.
long_description.en: Ördög, Ürdüng in Old Hungarian, is a form-changing demon of Hungarian myth and early paganism who commands the world's dark and evil powers. After Christianisation he was equated with the Devil. In Hungarian myth Isten, God, had Ördög's help in creating the world.

long_description.id: Ia agak mirip satir atau faun: tubuh atas lelaki dan tubuh bawah kambing, biasanya hitam pekat, berkuku belah, bertanduk domba, berekor panjang yang ujungnya seperti bilah, dan membawa garpu. Ia tinggal di dunia bawah atau neraka, Pokol, sambil terus mengaduk kuali besar berisi jiwa orang berdosa. Bila datang ke bumi ia bersembunyi di dinding rumah korbannya, atau menjelma rubah, nyala api gelap, atau gembala Hungaria bermata gelap berkilat; ia suka bertaruh dengan manusia untuk mengumpulkan jiwa.
long_description.en: He resembles a satyr or faun, man above and goat below, usually jet black, with cloven hooves, ram's horns, a long blade-tipped tail and a pitchfork. He lives in the underworld or hell, Pokol, forever stirring a vast cauldron of sinners' souls. On earth he may lurk inside his victims' walls making faint squeaks, or take the guise of a fox, a dark flame or a Hungarian herdsman whose dark eyes sparkle; he likes to wager with people in order to win their souls.

short_description.id: Pope Lick Monster adalah makhluk legenda urban setengah manusia setengah kambing yang konon tinggal di bawah jembatan kereta di Louisville, Kentucky.
short_description.en: The Pope Lick Monster is an urban-legend part-man, part-goat creature said to live under a railroad trestle in Louisville, Kentucky.

long_description.id: Pope Lick Monster, sering dijuluki Goat Man, adalah makhluk legendaris setengah manusia, setengah kambing dan domba yang konon hidup di bawah jembatan kereta di atas Pope Lick Creek di Louisville, Kentucky. Menurut sebagian kisah, ia memikat orang ke jembatan dengan hipnosis atau peniruan suara hingga tewas tertabrak kereta; kisah lain menyebut ia melompat ke atap mobil yang lewat.
long_description.en: The Pope Lick Monster, often called the Goat Man, is a legendary part-man, part-goat, part-sheep creature said to live under a railroad trestle over Pope Lick Creek in Louisville, Kentucky. Some accounts say it lures people onto the trestle with hypnosis or voice mimicry to be killed by trains; others say it leaps onto passing cars.

long_description.id: Satu legenda menyebut ia dulunya penampil sirkus yang membalas dendam setelah dianiaya. Legenda ini menarik pemburu sensasi, dan sudah terjadi sejumlah kematian serta kecelakaan di jembatan yang sebenarnya masih menjadi jalur kereta utama itu.
long_description.en: One legend says it was a mistreated circus performer seeking revenge. The legend draws thrill-seekers, and there have been several deaths and accidents on the trestle, which still carries a major rail line.

short_description.id: Ramidreju adalah hewan mitos Cantabria mirip musang bertubuh panjang seperti ular, lahir sekali tiap seratus tahun, yang bulunya menyembuhkan segala penyakit.
short_description.en: The ramidreju is a Cantabrian mythical weasel-like animal with a snake-long body, born once a century, whose fur cures every illness.

long_description.id: Ramidreju adalah makhluk mitologi Cantabria yang hidup di gunung dan hutan Spanyol utara. Hewan mirip musang ini lahir sekali setiap seratus tahun dari musang atau marten; tubuhnya panjang seperti ular, bulunya kehijauan, matanya kuning, dan dengan taring seperti babi hutan ia menggali lubang yang sangat dalam.
long_description.en: The ramidreju is a creature of Cantabrian mythology living in the mountains and forests of northern Spain. This weasel-like animal is born once every hundred years from a weasel or marten; it has a long snake-like body, greenish fur and yellow eyes, and digs very deep holes with boar-like tusks.

long_description.id: Ia sangat diburu karena bulunya menyembuhkan segala penyakit dan ia dapat membantu menemukan harta; menurut Manuel Llano, yang mendengarnya dari warga Viaña, empedunya diminum para anjana di lembah Cieza.
long_description.en: It is much hunted because its fur cures all ills and it can lead to treasure; according to Manuel Llano, who heard of it from a resident of Viaña, the anjanas of the Cieza valley drink its bile.

role.en: Its fur cures every illness.

short_description.id: Rougarou adalah manusia serigala dalam cerita rakyat Cajun, Kreol, dan Métis yang berkeliaran di rawa-rawa Louisiana, berkepala serigala atau anjing, dan dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak.
short_description.en: The rougarou is a werewolf of Cajun, Creole and Métis folklore that prowls the swamps of Louisiana with a wolf's or dog's head, used to frighten children into behaving.

long_description.id: Rougarou, dari kata Prancis loup-garou, adalah makhluk mirip manusia serigala dalam cerita rakyat Cajun dan Kreol di Louisiana serta komunitas Métis dan berbahasa Prancis di Kanada. Ia bertubuh manusia berkepala serigala atau anjing dan berkeliaran di rawa sekitar Acadiana dan New Orleans, ladang tebu, dan hutan; kisah lain menjadikannya penunggang tanpa kepala atau penyihir.
long_description.en: The rougarou, from French loup-garou, is a werewolf-like creature of Cajun and Creole folklore in Louisiana and of Métis and French-speaking communities in Canada. It has a human body and a wolf's or dog's head and prowls the swamps around Acadiana and New Orleans, cane fields and woods; other tales make it a headless horseman or a witch.

long_description.id: Kisahnya dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak. Menurut satu legenda kutukannya berlangsung 101 hari lalu berpindah ke orang yang darahnya ia tumpahkan, dan 13 benda kecil di depan pintu dapat menangkalnya karena ia tidak bisa menghitung lebih dari 12. Bagi orang Ojibwe, rugaru adalah lelaki berbulu pertanda bahaya. Ia muncul dalam serial Supernatural dan novel Empire of Wild.
long_description.en: Its tales were used to frighten children. One legend says its curse lasts 101 days and then passes to whoever's blood it draws, and 13 small objects by the door ward it off because it cannot count past 12. For the Ojibwe the rugaru is a hairy man who signals danger. It appears in the series Supernatural and the novel Empire of Wild.

claims.quote: alternatively spelled as roux-ga-roux, rugaroo, or rugaru) is a legendary creature in Cajun and Creole diaspora and a trickster in oral traditions in Métis and Francophone communities linked to traditional concepts of the werewolf.

statement.id: Rougarou (juga roux-ga-roux, rugaroo, atau rugaru) adalah makhluk legenda diaspora Cajun dan Kreol serta tokoh penipu dalam tradisi lisan komunitas Métis dan berbahasa Prancis, yang terkait dengan konsep manusia serigala.
statement.en: The rougarou (also roux-ga-roux, rugaroo or rugaru) is a legendary creature of the Cajun and Creole diaspora and a trickster in Métis and Francophone oral traditions, linked to the werewolf.

claims.quote: Loup is French for wolf, and garou (from Frankish warulf, cognate with English werewolf) is a man who transforms into an animal.

statement.id: Namanya dari loup-garou: loup berarti serigala dalam bahasa Prancis, dan garou (dari kata Franka warulf, sekerabat dengan werewolf) adalah manusia yang berubah menjadi binatang.
statement.en: The name comes from loup-garou: loup is French for wolf, and garou (from Frankish warulf, akin to werewolf) is a man who turns into an animal.

claims.quote: According to Barry Jean Ancelet, an academic expert on Cajun folklore and professor at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in America, the tale of the rougarou is a common legend across French Louisiana.

statement.id: Menurut Barry Jean Ancelet, pakar cerita rakyat Cajun di University of Louisiana at Lafayette, kisah rougarou adalah legenda umum di seluruh Louisiana berbahasa Prancis.
statement.en: According to Barry Jean Ancelet, Cajun folklore expert at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, the rougarou is a common legend across French Louisiana.

claims.quote: In the Creole and Cajun legends, the creature is said to prowl the swamps around Acadiana and Greater New Orleans, and the sugar cane fields and woodlands of the regions. The rougarou most often is described as a creature with a human body and the head of a wolf or dog, similar to the werewolf legend.

statement.id: Dalam legenda Kreol dan Cajun, rougarou berkeliaran di rawa-rawa sekitar Acadiana dan New Orleans serta ladang tebu dan hutan, dan biasanya bertubuh manusia berkepala serigala atau anjing.
statement.en: In Creole and Cajun legend the rougarou prowls the swamps around Acadiana and New Orleans and the cane fields and woods, usually with a human body and a wolf's or dog's head.

claims.quote: Often the story-telling has been used to inspire fear and obedience. One such example is stories that have been told by elders to persuade Creole and Cajun children to behave.

statement.id: Kisahnya sering dipakai untuk menanamkan rasa takut dan kepatuhan, misalnya oleh orang tua agar anak-anak Kreol dan Cajun berkelakuan baik.
statement.en: The tales were often used to instil fear and obedience, for instance by elders to make Creole and Cajun children behave.

claims.quote: A common blood sucking legend says that the rougarou is under the spell for 101 days. After that time, the curse is transferred from person to person when the rougarou draws another human's blood.

statement.id: Menurut legenda pengisap darah yang umum, rougarou berada di bawah kutukan selama 101 hari, lalu kutukan berpindah ke orang lain ketika rougarou menumpahkan darahnya.
statement.en: A common blood-drawing legend says the rougarou is under the spell for 101 days, after which the curse passes to another person whose blood the rougarou draws.

claims.quote: Some believe that placing 13 small objects by the door keeps the Rougarou at bay; the creature is said to be so simple-minded it can’t count beyond 12.

statement.id: Sebagian orang percaya meletakkan 13 benda kecil di dekat pintu dapat menangkal rougarou karena ia terlalu bodoh untuk menghitung lebih dari 12.
statement.en: Some believe that placing 13 small objects by the door keeps the rougarou away, since it is too simple to count past 12.

claims.quote: Rugaru is the Ojibwe name for "the hairy man who appears in symptom of danger or psychic disruption in the community."

statement.id: Rugaru adalah nama Ojibwe untuk "lelaki berbulu yang muncul sebagai tanda bahaya atau kekacauan batin dalam komunitas".
statement.en: Rugaru is the Ojibwe name for 'the hairy man who appears as a sign of danger or psychic disruption in the community'.

short_description.id: Sântoaderi adalah sekelompok makhluk gaib cerita rakyat Rumania berwujud pemuda berkuku kuda yang datang ke desa dengan nyanyian dan genderang, membawa penyakit dan menculik orang yang berada di luar rumah.
short_description.en: The Sântoaderi are a group of supernatural beings of Romanian folklore, hoofed young men who come to villages with song and drums, bringing illness and abducting anyone caught outdoors.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, Sântoaderi adalah rombongan tujuh atau sembilan pemuda berkaki panjang dan berkuku kuda yang mengenakan jubah. Mereka datang secara misterius ke desa, bernyanyi dan menabuh genderang, lalu membuat orang sakit dengan membelitnya dengan rantai hingga terkena rematik atau menginjak-injak tubuhnya.
long_description.en: In Romanian folklore the Sântoaderi are a band of seven or nine long-footed, hoofed young men wearing capes. They arrive mysteriously in a village, singing and beating drums, and make people ill by wrapping them in chains, causing rheumatism, or by stamping on their bodies.

long_description.id: Orang yang mendengar musik dan derap kuku mereka dianjurkan tetap di dalam rumah, karena di sana mereka aman. Orang yang tertinggal di luar bisa diculik dan dibawa ikut arak-arakan; sebagian kembali sehat dengan membawa hadiah, sebagian lagi kembali sakit, sekarat, atau gila.
long_description.en: People who heard their music and hoofbeats were advised to stay indoors, where they were safe. Anyone left outside could be abducted into the procession; some returned healthy with gifts, others sick, dying or insane.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus, dan mereka dipercaya lebih sering muncul pada hari rayanya. Mircea Eliade membandingkan Sântoaderi dengan zâne, yang juga berkelana pada malam hari dalam arak-arakan penari, dan konon pada hari ke-24 setelah Paskah kedua kelompok itu bertemu untuk bermain dan bertukar karangan bunga.
long_description.en: Their name derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, and they were thought most likely to appear on his feast day. Mircea Eliade compared the Sântoaderi with the zâne, who also travel by night in a procession of dancers, and on the 24th day after Easter the two groups are said to meet to play and exchange bouquets.

claims.quote: The Sântoaderi were a group of supernatural entities found in Romanian folklore. Viewed as either seven or nine young men with long feet and hooves, they were also thought of as wearing capes.

statement.id: Sântoaderi adalah sekelompok makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, dibayangkan sebagai tujuh atau sembilan pemuda berkaki panjang dan berkuku kuda (hooves), yang juga dianggap mengenakan jubah.
statement.en: The Sântoaderi were a group of supernatural beings of Romanian folklore, pictured as seven or nine young men with long feet and hooves, also thought to wear capes.

claims.quote: It was believed that they would mysteriously appear in a village, where they would sing, beat their drums, and cause illness for people; wrapping them up in chains causing rheumatism or stamping on their bodies.

statement.id: Diyakini mereka muncul secara misterius di sebuah desa, bernyanyi, menabuh genderang, dan membuat orang sakit: membelit mereka dengan rantai sehingga terkena rematik, atau menginjak-injak tubuh mereka.
statement.en: They were believed to appear mysteriously in a village, singing and beating drums, and to cause illness: wrapping people in chains, causing rheumatism, or stamping on their bodies.

claims.quote: Upon hearing their music and the sound of hooves, people were advised to stay indoors, which was considered safe. Those that did not retreat indoors, could be kidnapped by the Sântoaderi and made part of the procession.

statement.id: Begitu mendengar musik dan derap kuku mereka, orang dianjurkan tetap di dalam rumah, yang dianggap aman; yang tidak masuk rumah bisa diculik Sântoaderi dan dijadikan bagian dari arak-arakan mereka.
statement.en: On hearing their music and hoofbeats, people were advised to stay indoors, which was thought safe; those who did not could be kidnapped by the Sântoaderi and made part of their procession.

claims.quote: The victims of such kidnappings would sometimes return in healthy condition and carrying gifts; other times, they would return sick, dying, or insane.

statement.id: Korban penculikan itu kadang kembali dalam keadaan sehat sambil membawa hadiah, kadang kembali dalam keadaan sakit, sekarat, atau gila.
statement.en: Victims of such kidnappings sometimes came back healthy and carrying gifts, and at other times sick, dying or insane.

claims.quote: The name "Sântoader" derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, with folklore suggesting that the creatures were more likely to appear on his feast day.

statement.id: Nama "Sântoader" berasal dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus, dan menurut cerita rakyat makhluk ini lebih mungkin muncul pada hari rayanya.
statement.en: The name "Sântoader" derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, and folklore holds that the creatures were more likely to appear on his feast day.

statement.en: The Sântoaderi share some similarities with the fairies of Irish folklore; the Romanian historian Mircea Eliade also noted a resemblance between the Sântoaderi and the zîne, the Romanian equivalent of the fairy godmother.

claims.quote: Există, de asemenea, credința că în a 24-a zi după Paște, zânele și Sântoaderii se întâlnesc pentru a se juca și a-și oferi buchete de flori.

statement.id: Ada pula kepercayaan bahwa pada hari ke-24 setelah Paskah (a 24-a zi după Paște), zânele și Sântoaderii, yaitu para zâne dan Sântoaderi, bertemu untuk bermain dan saling memberi karangan bunga.
statement.en: There is also a belief that on the 24th day after Easter (a 24-a zi după Paște) the zânele și Sântoaderii, that is the zâne and the Sântoaderi, meet to play and give each other bouquets of flowers.

claims.quote: Istoricul român al religiilor Mircea Eliade a remarcat o asemănare între Sântoaderi și zâne, despre care se credea că, de asemenea, călătoresc noaptea într-un cortegiu de dansatoare.

statement.id: Sejarawan agama Rumania Mircea Eliade mencatat kemiripan antara Sântoaderi dan zâne, yang juga dipercaya berkelana pada malam hari dalam arak-arakan penari.
statement.en: The Romanian historian of religions Mircea Eliade noted a resemblance between the Sântoaderi and the zâne, who were also believed to travel by night in a procession of dancers.
